text:
maria: quick heads-up 52 onboarding sample app produced duplicated orders in two customer trials when clients hit 429s and immediately rotated tokens + retried. stack: node-sdk + hosted API. anyone else seen this?

kevin: saw a repro yesterday in sandbox. pattern: 429 -> client rotates token -> retry of original request happens without idempotency key -> duplicate created downstream.

sam: are we shipping any default Idempotency header in the sample app? i remember we kept it minimal on purpose.

maria: correct, no default idempotency header. we wanted minimal friction for new users but apparently that encourages copying insecure patterns.

tay: two quick angles: (A) add jittered backoff so retries are less likely to hit the server while token rotation is mid-flight, (B) default an idempotency-key in the sample to teach best practice.

kevin: sample app currently uses linear retries: 200ms, 500ms, 1000ms, no jitter. token refresh logic does an immediate re-auth and also triggers a retry path in parallel -> race.

sam: suggested plan: 1) sample app sets `Idempotency-Key` per logical operation (v4 uuid), 2) switch to exponential backoff with full jitter, 3) SDK/ sample add a small retry-queue handshake during token-rotation so queued retries wait for fresh token.

maria: for (1) we'll show server-side dedupe snippet too. important to demonstrate both client idempotency header and server dedupe behavior.

tay: for full jitter I'd prefer base=150ms. algorithm: sleep = random_between(0, base * 2^attempt). node snippet:```js
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms));
const backoff = (attempt) => Math.floor(Math.random() * (150 * Math.pow(2, attempt)));
await sleep(backoff(attempt));
```

kevin: good. also handle the auth-race: when SDK does refresh we should broadcast a `token.updated` event to the retry queue so retries rehydrate with the fresh token instead of replaying with the old one. that requires consistent behavior across node/python/go SDKs.

sam: telemetry additions: `retry.attempt` (fields: attempt_count, error_code, route, sampled), and `retry.duplicate_detected` when the server returns an idempotency conflict or when the client observes duplicate side-effect signals. sample app should expose counters at /metrics.

maria: agree. small sampling rule: capture full request/response payload for 1% of retried requests for debugging; always increment aggregated counters.

tay: we should add a tiny e2e script in the repo that reproduces the race: fuzz 429 responses, then force a token-rotation mid-retry. new hires can run it locally. call it `scripts/repro-429-token-race.sh`.

kevin: for SDK parity, open tasks: implement queued-retry handshake, add backoff util with full-jitter, add opt-out or opt-in idempotency key generator (sample app will opt-in by default). i'll prototype node+python this week and ping infra for a canary.

sam: devex-bot: add PR checklist for sample app changes: default `Idempotency-Key`, exponential+full-jitter backoff, retry-queue waits on token update, telemetry counters/events, server dedupe docs.

devex-bot: noted. assigning to @maria for sample app PR and @kevin for SDK changes. please paste PR links here when ready. :white_check_mark:

maria: i'll open a draft PR today with tests: small integration test that simulates 429 then token rotation and asserts no duplicate resource created. will update README: "sample app enables idempotency by default to demonstrate safe retries."

kevin: i'll send experimental SDK branches soon. can we also add a short guide in devex docs titled "Avoiding duplicate side-effects on 429+auth refresh" with code snippets for server-side dedupe?

sam: yes please. extra ask: include a tiny diagram showing the token refresh handshake and where retries should pause. helps onboarding folks grok the flow quickly.

maria: thanks all. i'll link PRs here. closing after merges. :sparkles:
